title: An invertible bifunctor comparison induces an invertible total-complex comparison
statement: Let $C_1,C_2,D,C_1^{\prime},C_2^{\prime},D^{\prime}$ be categories, with zero morphisms in the four $C$ categories and preadditive structures on $D,D^{\prime}$. Let $F:C_1\times C_2\to D$ and $F^{\prime}:C_1^{\prime}\times C_2^{\prime}\to D^{\prime}$ be bifunctors preserving zero morphisms in each variable, let $G_1:C_1\to C_1^{\prime}$ and $G_2:C_2\to C_2^{\prime}$ preserve zero morphisms, and let $G:D\to D^{\prime}$ be additive. Suppose $\tau_{Y,Z}:G(F(Y,Z))\to F^{\prime}(G_1Y,G_2Z)$ is natural in both variables and each component is invertible. For complex shapes $c_1,c_2,c$ admitting signed totalization and decidable equality on total degrees, let $K_1,K_2$ be complexes of shapes $c_1,c_2$. Assume both total complexes below exist and that $G$ preserves coproducts indexed by the pairs of bidegrees contributing to each total degree. Then the induced comparison $G(\operatorname{Tot}F(K_1,K_2))\to \operatorname{Tot}F^{\prime}(G_1K_1,G_2K_2)$ is invertible.

proof.text: In each total degree, the source after applying G is the coproduct of the images of the summands, because G preserves the indicated coproducts. The comparison sends each summand by its invertible component of tau to the corresponding summand of the target. Its inverse is the coproduct map induced by the inverse components. Checking on coproduct inclusions proves the inverse identities. Naturality of tau and additivity of G make the degreewise maps commute with the two differentials and their signs. A morphism of complexes invertible in every degree is invertible. This is precisely the existing proof in the recorded Lean source.
